root_cause: No execution feedback: first-draft SQL with over-specific/case-mismatched literals or wrong columns is returned unchecked
what: Add a draft-execute-verify-repair loop (max 2 calls): run the draft, and if it errors or returns zero rows, send the outcome plus sampled values of referenced string columns back for one corrected query; also strengthen the system prompt on LIKE/case-insensitive literal matching, choosing the right column among similarly named ones, and selecting full details when asked.
decision: s1 lifts evolve score from 83.33 to 90.0 with two fixes and zero regressions, and its draft-execute-verify-repair loop plus literal/column-matching guidance is a general text-to-SQL mechanism rather than task-specific patching; the ~450 extra tokens per task are justified by the gain and bounded by the 2-call cap.

root_cause: Blind single-shot generation: literal filters and output shape are never checked against the database, so silently-empty exact-match predicates go unrepaired
what: solve.py now executes the draft query and, when it errors, returns zero rows, or has an ambiguous projection ('details'/multi-table 'which X'), spends the second policy call on a repair message containing the error/row-count plus real stored values for each quoted literal probed from the schema. system_prompt.md gains general rules for LIKE-based literal matching, full-row output for 'details', symmetric friend relations and tie-aware LIMIT. config.json raises max_tokens so reasoning plus SQL is not truncated.

root_cause: Prompt rules actively push wrong semantics: anti-DISTINCT on fan-out joins, name-only projection for 'which X', and single-direction filters on symmetric relations
what: Rewrite system_prompt.md: (1) use SELECT DISTINCT when a 1:N join can repeat the requested entity unless individual event/enrolment records are asked; (2) for 'which <entities>' questions on attribute-rich tables return the full joined rows instead of only names; (3) for symmetric relations union both id columns before negation/aggregation. These target the exact error classes in sp0536, sp0755, sp0894 without touching control flow.

root_cause: Verification only reacts to errors/empty results, so silent semantic faults (join fan-out duplicates, one-direction-only filters on symmetric relations) are returned unchecked
what: Extend the verify step with two generic probes: a duplicate-row count probe on any non-DISTINCT multi-table draft (fan-out => ask for DISTINCT), and an opposite-direction probe that re-runs each equality predicate against the other column of its ON-joined pair; if that returns rows the draft missed, send both findings plus a short reminder (DISTINCT for entity sets, UNION both directions for symmetric relations, exact projection) back for one repair. Acceptance now also allows a successful repair of a suspicious-but-non-empty draft.

root_cause: Repair loop only fires on errors/zero rows, so silent semantic faults (join fan-out duplicates, wrong column for a symmetric relation) are never re-examined
what: Add two generic execution probes to the verify step: (a) wrap the draft in SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ...) — if the distinct count is lower than the row count and the question does not ask for individual records, trigger repair with that evidence; (b) when the draft filters on an id-like column, run a variant with every other same-type column of that table substituted as the filter column, and if exactly one alternative yields a different non-empty result, surface it as a candidate. Also add prompt rules about per-entity dedup on existence joins and choosing the subject-side column of a symmetric relation.
